title: Reproductive Comprehensive Set 1: Female Physiology - Oogenesis (Short Answer)

questions.prompt: At what period of life does the production of oogonia by mitotic division peak in the human female, and approximately how many cells are present at this peak?
questions.modelAnswer: Production peaks during fetal life (gestational weeks 20-24) at approximately 7 million oogonia.

questions.prompt: At what specific stage of meiosis are primary oocytes suspended from the time of birth until the moment of ovulation?
questions.modelAnswer: They are suspended in the prophase of the first meiotic division.

questions.prompt: Contrast the quantity of oocytes present in the ovaries at birth with the number remaining by the onset of puberty.
questions.modelAnswer: Approximately 2 million oocytes remain at birth, which declines to about 400,000 by puberty.

questions.prompt: Define the term "atresia" as it applies to the female reproductive lifespan.
questions.modelAnswer: The spontaneous regression and degeneration of ovarian follicles and their oocytes throughout the lifespan.

questions.prompt: Describe the basic structural composition of a primordial follicle.
questions.modelAnswer: A single primary oocyte surrounded by a layer of granulosa cells and stroma.

questions.prompt: During the first stage of follicular development, the primordial follicle becomes a primary follicle. Which two specific cell types proliferate to support and nurture the oocyte during this years-long phase?
questions.modelAnswer: Granulosa cells and theca interna cells.

questions.prompt: What is the "antrum," and during which stage of follicular development does it first appear?
questions.modelAnswer: A central cavity filled with fluid; it first appears during the second stage of follicular development (antral stage).

questions.prompt: Identify the specific components found within the fluid that accumulates in the antrum of a secondary follicle.
questions.modelAnswer: Steroid hormones, follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), proteins, and mucopolysaccharides.

questions.prompt: At what precise point in the 28-day menstrual cycle is the first meiotic division completed, and what is the name of the resulting oocyte?
questions.modelAnswer: It is completed just prior to ovulation; the resulting cell is the secondary oocyte.

questions.prompt: Under what specific condition does a secondary oocyte complete its second meiotic division?
questions.modelAnswer: The oocyte only completes the second meiotic division if it is successfully fertilized by a sperm.

questions.prompt: Describe the selection process of the "dominant follicle" that occurs during the third stage of follicular development.
questions.modelAnswer: Approximately 5-7 days after menses, a single Graafian follicle achieves dominance over its cohorts, which then undergo atresia.

questions.prompt: What endocrine structure is formed from the residual elements of the ruptured follicle immediately following ovulation?
Identify the four primary histological components that make up the corpus luteum.
questions.modelAnswer: Granulosa cells, theca cells, capillaries, and fibroblasts.

questions.prompt: If fertilization does not occur, what is the fate of the corpus luteum, and what is the name of the resulting scar tissue?
questions.modelAnswer: It regresses (involutes) at the end of the luteal phase and becomes a white scar called the corpus albicans.

questions.prompt: Explain the fundamental difference between the production of gametes in males versus the oocyte supply available to a female at birth.
questions.modelAnswer: Males produce spermatogonia and spermatocytes continuously throughout life, while females are born with a fixed, declining pool of oocytes and do not produce new oogonia after the fetal period.
